selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with acute urinary retention, hematemesis, progressive neurological deficits, and the development of marked paraparesis, along with the MRI findings of multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions and diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the spinal cord, supports the diagnosis of Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM). The presence of normal sensory function, hypertonic sphincters, and hyperalgesia also aligns with ADEM. While Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD) is a close runner-up due to the involvement of the spinal cord and brainstem, the lack of specific antibodies and the presence of more widespread lesions favor ADEM.

rejected.label: Toxic Encephalopathy
rejected.why: Lack of specific toxic exposure and more focal neurological deficits

rejected.label: Acute Transverse Myelitis
rejected.why: Involvement of the brain and more extensive spinal cord lesions

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis (MS)
rejected.why: Acute onset and lack of previous episodes
